episode.title: Cariboo Signals - Arts, Culture & Digital Storytelling
episode.description:
Riley and Casey explore technology and society in rural communities. Today's focus: Arts, Culture & Digital Storytelling.

NEWS ROUNDUP: We break down The Hair Dryer Question and Tod Maffin, plus 1 more stories, and explore what these developments mean for communities like ours.

RURAL CONNECTIONS: Should small arts organizations in rural areas prioritize platform-native vertical video distribution, or invest in community-owned digital archives with clips as secondary marketing? Topics include: Platform homogenization vs. format as neutral distribution tool, Cold-start problem for rural artists without established credibility, Preservation vs. discovery in digital archives, How algorithmic pressure reshapes creative output (songwriting, performance structure), Community-owned infrastructure as alternative to platform dependency.

Hosts: Riley (Tech optimist with an engineering background) and Casey (Community-first skeptic of tech promises).

COMMUNITY SPOTLIGHT: Central Cariboo Arts & Culture Society

discussion.central_question: Should small arts organizations in rural areas prioritize platform-native vertical video distribution, or invest in community-owned digital archives with clips as secondary marketing?
discussion.riley_position: Vertical video is a necessary distribution tool that reaches new audiences; the key is treating it as a door to the work, not the work itself, while maintaining independent archives as the durable master record.
riley_key_evidence: HubSpot report showing vertical short-form is the most-used and successful content format in marketing
Tod Maffin's model of consistent weekly output on controlled platforms building genuine, durable reach over years
Netflix expanding vertical video formats because audiences have already moved to that consumption pattern
discussion.casey_position: Platform-dependent distribution restructures artistic production around algorithmic incentives and creates preservation risk; community-owned master recordings should be the primary goal, with platform clips as optional secondary exports only.
casey_key_evidence: Most viral impressions evaporate without converting to ticket sales or audience building—vertical video builds impressions, not durable audiences
Commercial pop songwriting has restructured itself around algorithmic skip windows and streaming metrics, showing how platform pressure reshapes creative work itself
Rural creators face a cold-start problem that cheaper tools don't solve—established credibility still matters more than format accessibility
discussion.resolution: They reached partial agreement: own the full-length recording first as the durable asset, treat vertical clips as disposable secondary marketing, and recommend a testable one-camera experiment for the Arts Centre without waiting for permission or funding. Casey conceded the packaging framing but insisted the preservation problem must be solved before discovery, while Riley acknowledged organizational discipline is critical to preventing metrics-driven mission drift.
